Definition: from λοιδός (mischief); abusive, i.e. a blackguard:--railer, reviler.
BiblicalUsage: loídoros means railer, reviler, and once is enough to see what it is doing. In 1 Corinthians 6:10, "nor revilers"; and in 1 Corinthians 5:11, "or a railer".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the reviler is named among those who shall not inherit the kingdom — not to shame the struggling, but to warn the church whom it must not keep company with.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
